newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly up.
newsitem.headline: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly up.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Monday issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing
prices and are annual percentage rates.
Turnover fell sharply to 2.407 billion yuan from 5.084 billion yuan last Friday with the seven-day contract the most actively traded.
The fall in volume was mainly due to less trading by the head offices of state-owned banks, traders said.
Short-term financial centres, the money brokerages run by the central bank, continue to trade actively with the Beijing centre the biggest lender, they said.
This was partly due to active borrowing of non-banking financial institutions including the securities houses, who needed money to trade on the bubbling domestic A share markets.
Traders said China's fixed asset investment had increased considerably so far this year, which would support the interbank rates in the short term with money demand expected to stay strong.
They said they expected the rates to move steadily around the current level in the next few days.
